occupants.note: ADOPTED BY THE INFERRED-HOUSEHOLD PROGRAMME (docs/ROADMAP.md K1, phase two). This anonymous roof is the dwelling of an inferred butcher's household (1 of 1 this layer infers): hh_inf_butcher_south_01 in data/residents/households/. THE ROOF'S OWN EXISTENCE, POSITION AND FOOTPRINT REMAIN CONJECTURAL and are unchanged by the adoption; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit. The occupant is hypothesised from the town's demonstrable needs - the 1835 census of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings against the trades Andreas's 1833 roster names - and is not a person: no name is claimed and no figure is drawn.

residents.name: An inferred butcher's household (south division)
residents.why: THE HOUSEHOLD IS HOUSED, WHICH IS THE POINT OF THE LAYER. recon_1835_south_d5_011 is an anonymous inferred roof already standing on the plat, adopted rather than duplicated: its existence, position and footprint stay conjectural and the adoption adds only the occupant argument. Which roof of the right family and district a hypothesised household occupies is not evidence about that roof; the household needed a dwelling and the programme assigned it one.
residents.basis: An anonymous roof of the reconstruction programme, ADOPTED by this household rather than raised for it. The roof's own existence and position stay conjectural; what the adoption adds is an argued occupant instead of an anonymous count-unit.

persons.name: A butcher (inferred resident, unnamed)
persons.note: HYPOTHESISED, AND NOT A PERSON. No source names this resident and none is claimed to: the record asserts that a town of 3,265 people in 398 dwellings held at least this many households of this trade, and asserts nothing whatever about any individual. The name field carries a designation because inventing a surname would make this record indistinguishable at a glance from the documented layer beside it. No figure is drawn (docs/LIBERTIES.md L1). THE FIRST OF 1 BUTCHER HOUSEHOLDS THIS LAYER INFERS. One butcher is documented: Clybourne, the government butcher, who is also a packer and lives three kilometres out on the North Branch. A town of 3,265 buys fresh meat daily and does not walk to the North Branch for it. One butchering household is inferred, keeping a market shop on the built streets.

residents.research_note: INFERRED HOUSEHOLD - first of 1 butcher households in this layer, in the south division. One butcher is documented: Clybourne, the government butcher, who is also a packer and lives three kilometres out on the North Branch. A town of 3,265 buys fresh meat daily and does not walk to the North Branch for it. One butchering household is inferred, keeping a market shop on the built streets. METHOD: the count comes from the occupation census in data/reconstruction/1835_inferred_household_programme.json, which calibrates every trade against three things this project already holds - the 1835 town census (3,265 people, 398 dwellings), Andreas's roster of the fall of 1833 (about fifty named people, most with a trade, in a settlement of some 350), and the reconstruction specification's roof schedule, whose workshop and store family targets are treated as the ceiling on a trade rather than as its measure. Every count is stated NET of the documented layer: this dataset infers a tradesman only where it cannot name one.
